title: Lesson 4: Digital Citizenship — Being Christlike Online
subtitle: How to Honor God in Every Digital Interaction
key_concepts: Being a light in digital spaces

verses.text: "And whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him."
verses.commentary: This verse applies to our online behavior just as much as our offline behavior. Every comment we post, every message we send, and every image we share should be done in a way that honors Jesus.

verses.text: "Do not let any unwholesome talk come out of your mouths, but only what is helpful for building others up according to their needs, that it may benefit those who listen."
verses.commentary: Our words online carry real weight. Unkind comments, gossip, and hurtful messages are just as sinful as saying those things face-to-face. God calls us to use our words — including our typed words — to build others up.

verses.text: "In the same way, let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven."
verses.commentary: The digital world is a mission field. How we behave online is a witness to others. We can be a light in the darkness by showing kindness, truth, and grace in our digital interactions.

content.heading: Introduction: What Is Digital Citizenship?
paragraphs: Digital citizenship means behaving responsibly and ethically whenever you use technology. Just as being a good citizen in your community means following laws, treating others with respect, and contributing positively, being a good digital citizen means doing the same things online.

As Christians, we are called to an even higher standard. We do not just follow rules — we follow Christ. Everything we do online should reflect His character: love, truth, patience, kindness, and self-control.

content.heading: Communicating Online
paragraphs: One of the biggest challenges of online communication is that it removes the face-to-face element. You cannot see the other person's expression or hear their tone of voice. This makes it easy to misunderstand others and easy to say things you would never say in person.

Before you post a comment, send a message, or reply to someone online, ask yourself: Would I say this to the person's face? Would I be proud if my parents or my pastor read this? Does this reflect the love of Christ? If the answer to any of these questions is no, do not post it.

content.heading: Cyberbullying and Standing Up for Others
paragraphs: Cyberbullying is using technology to harass, threaten, or humiliate someone. It can include mean messages, spreading rumors, sharing embarrassing photos, or excluding someone from online groups. Cyberbullying is a sin because it violates God's command to love our neighbors as ourselves.

If you see cyberbullying happening, do not participate or stay silent. Be brave enough to stand up for the person being bullied. Report the behavior to a trusted adult. You may be the only person willing to show kindness in that moment, and your courage can make a real difference.

content.heading: Being a Light in Digital Spaces
paragraphs: The internet can be a dark place, filled with negativity, anger, and dishonesty. But Jesus calls His followers to be lights in the darkness. You can be a light online by sharing encouraging words, being honest and respectful in your interactions, and refusing to participate in gossip or cruelty.

Remember that real people with real feelings are behind every screen. Treat everyone you interact with online as someone made in the image of God — because they are. Your digital footprint is a record of how you treated people, and it should reflect the love of Christ.

reflection_questions.question: What does it mean to be a digital citizen? How is being a Christian digital citizen different from just following the rules?
reflection_questions.guidance: Think about the difference between external compliance and heart-level obedience. Consider how Christ's example goes beyond just rule-following.

reflection_questions.question: How does Ephesians 4:29 apply to what you write online? Give an example of a comment that builds up and one that tears down.
reflection_questions.guidance: Think about specific online situations — social media comments, group chats, or gaming interactions. Consider the impact of words even when spoken from behind a screen.

reflection_questions.question: What should you do if you witness cyberbullying? Why does staying silent make you part of the problem?
reflection_questions.guidance: Consider what the Bible says about standing up for the weak and oppressed. Think about practical steps you can take to help.
